newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress says want to avoid polls.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress says want to avoid polls.

text.p: The president of India's Congress party, Sitaram Kesri, said on Saturday that his party's top priority was to avoid elections after the fall of the United Front coalition government.

"The first priority is to avoid elections," Kesri told Reuters by telephone in the Indian capital. The Congress leader said negotiations with the United Front on a possible new government would start later on Saturday.

Congress provoked the fall of the United Front government by withdrawing its support for the centre-left coalition on March 30, and had earlier said it wanted to stake a claim to form a fresh government.
However, asked if he would ask President Shankar Dayal Sharma for the right to form a new government, Kesri said: "That is not the most important issue."
Sitaram Yechury, a member of the United Front's decision-making steering committee, told Reuters that caretaker prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's alliance also did not want elections.
"There is an overwhelming demand for a need to avoid elections. So we are meeting at the United Front to try to form a government."
